correctness.rationale: Exact voter-arrow duality gives k^2/r death rate for k coalescing ancestral walkers on the peripheral clique; the strong Markov property gives the full independent-exponential law. Factorial residues give the finite exact CDF. Uniform |a_{r,j}|<=2 and normalized spectral gap between 1 and 4 yield m-tail convergence O_x(m^-3) uniformly in r. Uniform two-sided integrable tails justify the mean. An independent forward birth-death generator, rational resolvent and characteristic-polynomial verifier passed 155 checks at r=1,...,10, providing nonproof cross-checks. Assumptions include rate-one node update and all nonhub spins initially negative.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The star result is a strict boundary specialization, not a dominating theorem. Both clique-bouquet flooding works concern independent exponential bond passage with infection cut rates j(r+1-j); their double minimal eigenvalues and loglog shift cannot imply the single-minimum rate j^2/r law for the voter model. General extremal phase-type theory might subsume the abstract maximum after independent derivation of uniform residues, which remains a residual historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: The exact full absorption-time law and uniform two-parameter extreme-value theorem quantify consensus kinetics on a canonical clique-bouquet graph family. More importantly, they show that choosing voter imitation instead of independent edge transmission on identical geometry removes the otherwise necessary loglog m shift, mechanistically explained by one versus two slow modes. The observable and comparison are natural to interacting-particle systems, and the universal-in-r estimate is stronger than isolated fixed-network examples.
